name: HIV-associated Cancer

criteria.description: Histopathological confirmation of malignancy in the context of HIV infection
Confirmed HIV seropositivity by ELISA and Western blot or PCR
Presence of characteristic clinical features such as Kaposi sarcoma lesions, lymphoma masses, or invasive cervical cancer

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Confirmed HIV infection plus histopathological evidence of malignancy consistent with HIV-associated cancer
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of non-HIV-related malignancies and consideration of immune status

searchTerms: purple skin lesions typical of Kaposi sarcoma

pathognomonic.notes: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma presenting with painless lymph node enlargement
searchTerms: persistent swollen lymph nodes with lymphoma
enlarged lymph nodes due to lymphoma

common.symptomName: Unexplained weight loss exceeding 10% body weight
common.notes: Common systemic symptom in HIV-associated malignancies
searchTerms: losing more than 10% body weight without cause

common.notes: White patches on lateral tongue associated with Epstein-Barr virus

common.symptomName: Persistent cough with or without hemoptysis
common.notes: May indicate pulmonary lymphoma or Kaposi sarcoma involvement
searchTerms: ongoing cough with or without blood

occasional.symptomName: Neurological deficits due to CNS lymphoma
occasional.notes: Focal neurological signs or cognitive decline
searchTerms: neurological symptoms due to CNS tumor

occasional.symptomName: Abdominal pain or mass from visceral lymphoma
occasional.notes: May indicate intra-abdominal lymphadenopathy or organ involvement
searchTerms: belly pain or lump from internal lymphoma

occasional.notes: May be related to gastrointestinal lymphoma or opportunistic infections

occasional.symptomName: Dyspnea due to pleural effusion or pulmonary Kaposi sarcoma
searchTerms: shortness of breath from lung or pleural disease
breathing difficulty due to lung involvement
dyspnea from chest fluid or tumor

rare.symptomName: Visual disturbances from ocular Kaposi sarcoma
searchTerms: vision problems from eye Kaposi sarcoma

laboratory: HIV viral load and CD4+ T-cell count indicating immunosuppression
imaging: CT or MRI showing lymphadenopathy or mass lesions
Chest X-ray with pulmonary infiltrates or effusions
PET scan demonstrating hypermetabolic tumor sites
genetic: Detection of Epstein-Barr virus DNA in lymphoma tissue
HHV-8 (Human herpesvirus 8) DNA in Kaposi sarcoma lesions
other: Bone marrow biopsy in suspected lymphoma

distinguishingFeatures: Histopathology may differ in subtype and viral associations

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging lymph nodes or masses
New onset of neurological deficits in HIV-positive patient
Unexplained persistent fever and weight loss
references: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. HIV/AIDS and Cancer. CDC.gov.
National Comprehensive Cancer Network. Guidelines for HIV-Associated Malignancies, 2024.
Gopal S, et al. HIV-associated cancers and their management. Lancet Oncol. 2023.
